quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Photomask business plan (Nakanishi, head of Fine Device Operations): DNP aims for average annual photomask sales growth of more than 15% through FY2030 (the fiscal year ending March 2031), driven by commercialising cutting-edge technologies. After JPY20 billion of capex in April 2023 - March 2026 it is raising its photomask capex plan for April 2026 - March 2029 to JPY70 billion, covering EUV masks, nanoimprint and production capability from advanced areas to the volume zone, and expects sales in cutting-edge areas alone to rise by JPY24 billion in the year ending March 2029 versus the year ended March 2025. Management (Q&A): it cannot break down the JPY70 billion, but as EUV equipment is extremely expensive EUV accounts for a substantial proportion; capex for nanoimprint mass production is not yet included and will be decided once customers indicate production timing and volumes; the large photomask sales increase projected in its materials for the years ending March 2028 and March 2029 reflects capacity expansion through large-scale capex; growth is now forecast above last year's plan because EUV-related business has become more tangible and merchant sales volume is expected to be greater than anticipated last year, from higher order volumes at existing customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Photomask sales growth more than 15% a year through FY2030 (year ending March 2031); photomask capex JPY 70 billion (April 2026 - March 2029); cutting-edge sales +JPY 24 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: EUV and nanoimprint status (Nakanishi): DNP 'successfully completed Rapidus' NEDO (New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization) project as planned' and, building on that experience, has established the technical capabilities and manufacturing foundation for 2 nm-generation EUV masks; it aims to be a partner with reliable supply capacity in advanced masks, including EUV masks, as device makers outsource advanced logic and memory photomasks. In nanoimprint it has developed a 10 nm line-width template equivalent to the 1.4 nm generation, now under evaluation by several customers, and will keep expanding its presence 'as the sole mask supplier'. Management says these technologies come from more than 10 years of R&D and upfront investment and from collaboration with partners including KIOXIA, Rapidus, imec and Canon, plus long-standing photomask joint ventures.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 nm-generation EUV mask capability established; 10 nm line-width nanoimprint template (1.4 nm generation) in evaluation by several customers

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Photomask demand view (Nakanishi; management Q&A): DNP expects the semiconductor market to grow from about USD770 billion in 2025 to about USD2 trillion in 2035 (about 10% a year), driven by AI semiconductors for data centers, advanced logic and advanced memory; in the merchant photomask market, advanced-node demand expands significantly as miniaturisation needs more masks, while the over-14 nm volume segment grows steadily. Customers putting their limited resources into cutting-edge products outsource previous-generation masks, and DNP expects outsourcing of products one or two generations behind the leading edge to increase rapidly; even EUV processes include non-EUV layers that customers will outsource, and high-end optical masks at the EUV boundary will be progressively outsourced. EUV demand 'has yet to take off', but demand is rising steadily in the high-resolution segment for the generation immediately preceding EUV, where DNP is securing orders; legacy-node masks were affected by reduced smartphone production due to memory shortages, but DNP is securing orders for industrial and automotive applications. AI investment, now extending to physical AI, is expected to lift orders for both EUV masks and related non-EUV layers; DNP will meet staffing needs by reallocating people across the group as well as hiring.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor market from about USD 770 billion (2025) to about USD 2 trillion (2035), about 10% a year

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Group plan detail (Senior Managing Director Miyake; management Q&A): operating profit is to grow about 9% a year from JPY101 billion (year ended March 2026) to JPY130 billion (year ending March 2029). Half of sales in the year to March 2026 came from the six focus businesses, which are to reach 57% by the year to March 2029, while businesses for reforming fall from 48% (year to March 2023) and 17% to 9%; the six focus businesses' total sales are to grow about 10% a year, from JPY510 billion (year to March 2023) and JPY606 billion (year to March 2026) to JPY808 billion (year to March 2029), with information security going from JPY187 billion to JPY271 billion (13% CAGR). More than 60% of the JPY200 billion growth capex goes to Electronics, especially semiconductors; because EUV, nanoimprint and glass cores are set to enter the mass-production phase during April 2026 - March 2029, DNP plans continued capex and possibly further capacity investment. Q&A: capex is not fixed at JPY200 billion and, through flexible allocation, semiconductor growth investment could exceed JPY120 billion. Structural reforms are to add JPY5 billion or more in the year ending March 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Focus businesses 57% of sales by the year ending March 2029; more than 60% of JPY 200 billion growth capex to Electronics; semiconductor growth investment could exceed JPY 120 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Digital Interface (Miyake): its main products are metal masks, increasingly for OLED, and optical films. Because of the semiconductor memory shortage some manufacturers find it difficult to produce smartphones in the short term, so DNP's metal-mask order volume is declining; smartphone OLED panel shipments are projected to decline in what DNP labels FY2026 and grow about 3% a year thereafter. Foldables could raise the OLED area per phone about three times, lifting metal-mask shipments; notebook PCs and tablets are forecast to grow about 29% a year and TV screens of 65 inches and larger about 6% a year in area. DNP will use its G8-size production line across more OLED panel types and raise utilisation of the line installed last September mainly for surface materials for 65-inch and larger panels; the goal is about 5% average annual sales growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Digital Interface sales goal about 5% a year; notebook PC and tablet market about 29% a year

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Smart Communication businesses: information security (Numano, Information Innovation Operations) - after consolidating Rubicon SEZC (government ID, focused on Africa) in July 2025, DNP announced a tender offer for AUSTRIACARD HOLDINGS AG on May 13, 2026 (customer base in Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Africa and North America in financial and government ID) to combine DNP's Asian, Rubicon's African and AUSTRIACARD's platforms with a focus on government IDs and ID authentication; the domestic digital ID and authentication market is expected to grow at a 7.8% CAGR; sales are planned to grow from 100 in FY2024 (year ended March 2025) to 167 by FY2030, about 8.9% a year. Photo imaging (Murakami, Imaging Communications Operations) - more than 400,000 DNP printers operate in over 100 countries, producing about 5 billion photo prints a year, with manufacturing in Japan, the US, Malaysia and the Netherlands; an India subsidiary began sales in March 2026; sales are to grow from 100 in FY2024 to 129 by 2030 (4.4% a year) and profit to 175 (9.9% a year) through higher-value-added printers and media such as the DS820DX launched in 2024; 4-inch prints are about 80% of volume.
quarterly_data.figure: Information security sales index 100 (FY2024) to 167 (FY2030); photo imaging profit index to 175 by 2030 (9.9% CAGR)

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Life & Healthcare businesses (Miyake; Tsuchiya, Medical & Healthcare; management Q&A): mobility & living - the Hikari Kinzoku acquisition expands in-vehicle HMI, mass production of decorative films for car roofs as a paint alternative has begun, Artellion aluminium panels are being expanded overseas; sales plan about 11% a year. Industrial high-performance materials - battery pouches focus on ESS in the interim (mass production already under way for some products; ESS pouches scheduled for mass production in the year ending March 2027) while automotive stays challenging; DNP is in the early stages of launching a US business in photovoltaic-related components, particularly to meet demand from AI data centers; sales plan 12% a year from the year to March 2025 through the year to March 2031; a production line at the Tsuruse Plant (Saitama) for electrified-vehicle pouches may start operating within the next three years. Medical & healthcare - a CDMO business built on CMIC CMO (50.1% acquired in April 2023; four domestic and two overseas sites), drug substances, healthcare packaging and AI/DX (Clinical Trial Sync launched July 1); sales CAGR above 5% and profit CAGR above 20% by 2030.

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Glass-core status (Nakanishi, head of Fine Device Operations): semiconductor makers and package-substrate makers are conducting full-scale evaluations with a view to mass production; DNP completed a glass-core pilot line at its Kuki Plant (Saitama) at the end of 2025, has begun evaluation activities, and is collaborating with a leading package substrate manufacturer on technical validation in preparation for mass production. The market's adoption schedule is under careful review and the start of mass production 'has been pushed back from the previously anticipated 2028 to 2030', which DNP sees as a shift from the demonstration phase to evaluation for mass-production applications rather than a decline. DNP plans to build a mass-production system gradually in line with customers and expects to decide on the first phase - an investment of JPY30 billion - sometime in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: First-phase glass-core investment JPY 30 billion, decision expected in 2026; market mass production pushed from 2028 to 2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing IR Day: DNP Group IR-Day FY2026 (07-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Glass-core market and targets (Nakanishi; management Q&A): high-performance semiconductors expected to incorporate glass cores, such as AI accelerators and CPUs, are projected to grow about 20% a year, and package sizes are rising fast - particularly after 2028 - so glass cores will be needed where conventional materials are no longer sufficient. DNP targets the high-aspect-ratio, high-quality segment, building on partnerships with leading package-substrate makers and its plating, precision patterning and design technologies; it plans to enter next-generation advanced packaging centred on glass cores in the medium term and optoelectronic integration in the long term. Management anticipates glass-core sales of JPY30 billion or more in FY2032 (the fiscal year ending March 2033), with contributions starting in the near term as the business ramps up, and answered 'your understanding is correct' when asked whether that means about JPY5 billion in FY2029 (year ending March 2030) and about JPY35 billion in FY2032. Strengths it claims: void-free copper filling of the holes formed in glass, smaller holes relative to substrate thickness (aspect ratio) at higher hole density, and long experience handling thin glass substrates up to three meters square from its color-filter business. The glass-core business is classed as a growth-potential business.
quarterly_data.figure: Glass-core sales JPY 30 billion or more in FY2032 (fiscal year ending March 2033); about JPY 5 billion in FY2029 (year ending March 2030)
